en: The Scripture on the Ten Paths of Wholesome Action, translated by the Tripitaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan during the Great Tang Dynasty, by imperial decree.
Thus have I heard: At one time the Buddha was dwelling in the palace of the Dragon King Sāgara, together with eight thousand great [bodhisattvas].
The assembly of bhikṣus was together with thirty-two thousand bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Dragon King, saying:
"Because the mental conceptions of all sentient beings differ, the karma they create also differs; it is for this reason that there is the revolving through the various realms of existence."
"O Dragon King!
Do you see that the forms, colors, and species within this assembly and within the great ocean are each distinct?
All such things are brought about by nothing other than the mind’s creation of wholesome and unwholesome actions of body, speech, and mind."
Yet the mind has no form and cannot be seen or grasped; it is merely a collection of illusory phenomena arising together, ultimately devoid of a master, and lacking a self or what belongs to a self.
Although what appears differs according to the respective karma of each being, in reality there is no agent within it.
Therefore, all phenomena are inconceivable, their intrinsic nature being like an illusion.

Once the wise have understood this, they should cultivate wholesome karma; by means of this, the aggregates, sense bases, and elements that arise will all be perfectly upright and beautiful, such that those who behold them never grow weary.
“Nāga King! Behold the Buddha’s body, born from hundreds of thousands of millions of merits, adorned with all the marks, its radiance so brilliant that it eclipses the entire assembly;
even the countless billions of sovereign Brahmā kings no longer appear before it.”
Those who gaze upon the body of the Tathāgata cannot help but have their eyes dazzled!
Furthermore, observe these great bodhisattvas, whose wondrous forms are adorned and pure; all of them have arisen from the cultivation and accumulation of wholesome karma and merit.
Furthermore, those among the devas, nāgas, and the eight classes of beings who possess great majestic power are likewise born from the merit of virtuous karma.

As for all the sentient beings currently within the great ocean—whether their forms and colors are coarse or base, large or small—they all arise from the various conceptualizations of their own minds as they perform unwholesome actions of body, speech, and mind; therefore, each receives their retribution according to their respective karma.
You should now train yourself in this way, and you should also cause all sentient beings to thoroughly understand cause and effect and cultivate wholesome karma.
You should remain unshakable in this right view, never again falling into the extremes of nihilism or eternalism, and you should joyfully honor and provide for those who are fields of merit!
For this reason, you too shall receive the respect and offerings of humans and devas. "Dragon King!
You should know that there is one dharma of a bodhisattva which can sever all suffering in the various evil realms."
What is this one thing?

It is to constantly recollect, contemplate, and examine wholesome dharmas throughout the day and night, causing all wholesome dharmas to increase with every thought-moment, allowing not even a hair’s breadth of unwholesome states to intermingle.

This is precisely that which enables the eternal severance of all evils and the perfection of wholesome dharmas (*kuśala-dharma*), and allows one to constantly draw near to the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and other noble assemblies.

As for what are called "wholesome dharmas," they refer to the bodies of humans and devas, the enlightenment of Śrāvakas, the enlightenment of Pratyekabuddhas, and unsurpassed enlightenment; since all these rely on this dharma as their fundamental basis to achieve fulfillment, they are named "wholesome dharmas."
This Dharma is precisely the ten paths of wholesome action.
What are these ten? They are:
being able to forever abstain from killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, false speech, divisive speech, harsh speech, frivolous speech, covetousness, ill will, and wrong views.
“Nāga King! If one abstains from taking life, one will immediately achieve the ten dharmas that eliminate affliction. What are these ten?
First, universally bestowing fearlessness upon all sentient beings;
second, constantly giving rise to a mind of great compassion toward sentient beings;
third, forever severing all habitual tendencies of anger and malice.
Fourth, the body is always free from illness;
fifth, one’s lifespan is long and far-reaching;
sixth, one is constantly protected by non-human beings.
Seventh, one will never have bad dreams and will experience joy upon waking from sleep;
eighth, enmities and knots will be extinguished, and all enemies will naturally reconcile;
ninth, there will be no fear of the evil realms.
Tenth, at the end of life, one is reborn in the heavens.

These are the ten; if one can dedicate these merits toward Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, then upon attaining Buddhahood in the future, one will obtain the Buddha’s lifespan of sovereign mastery over the mind.
"Furthermore, Dragon King!
If one abstains from stealing, one will obtain ten kinds of qualities that inspire confidence. What are these ten?
First, one's accumulated wealth cannot be dissipated by kings, thieves, water, fire, or unwelcome heirs;
second, one is cherished and remembered by many people;
third, one is not deceived or oppressed by others.
4. Praised by all directions;
5. Free from anxiety regarding harm;
6. One's good reputation spreads abroad.
Seventh, fearlessness when amidst a multitude;
eighth, being fully endowed with and lacking nothing in wealth, life-span, physical appearance, strength, happiness, and eloquence;
ninth, constantly maintaining a mind intent on giving.
Tenth, at the end of life, one is reborn in the heavens.
These are the ten. If one can dedicate these merits toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, then upon attaining Buddhahood in the future, one will realize the pure wisdom of great *bodhi*.
"Furthermore, O Dragon King!
If one abstains from sexual misconduct, one immediately attains four kinds of dharmas praised by the wise. What are these four?
First, the faculties are well-tamed and compliant;
second, one is forever free from clamor and agitation;
third, one is praised by the world.
Fourth, his wife cannot be violated by others.

These are the four; if one can dedicate these merits toward Anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, then at the time of attaining Buddhahood, one will obtain the mark of the Buddha’s secret male organ being concealed within a sheath.
"Furthermore, O Dragon King!
If one abstains from false speech, one immediately attains eight qualities praised by the devas.
What are these eight?
First, his mouth is always pure, with the fragrance of the *utpala* lotus;
second, he is trusted and revered by all the world;
third, his words are taken as authoritative testimony, and he is respected and loved by humans and devas.
Fourth, they constantly comfort sentient beings with kind speech;
fifth, they attain a superior intentionality, such that their three karmas are pure;
sixth, their speech is free from error, and their minds are always joyful.
Seventh, his speech is honored, and humans and devas follow its precepts;
eighth, his wisdom is preeminent, and none can subdue it. These are the eight.
If one can dedicate these toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, then upon attaining Buddhahood in the future, one will immediately possess the Tathāgata’s words of truth.
"Furthermore, Dragon King!
If one abstains from divisive speech, one will immediately attain five kinds of indestructible qualities. What are these five?
First, they attain an indestructible body, because nothing can harm it;
second, they attain an indestructible retinue, because nothing can break it apart;
third, they attain indestructible faith, because it accords with their original karma.
Fourth, one attains the practice of indestructible dharmas, because that which is cultivated is firm and solid;
fifth, one attains indestructible spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*), because they do not deceive or mislead.

These are the five. If one can dedicate these toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, then at the time of later attaining Buddhahood, one will obtain a true retinue that cannot be thwarted or destroyed by any demons or heterodox teachers.
"Furthermore, Dragon King!
If one abandons harsh speech, one will immediately achieve eight kinds of pure karma.
What are these eight?
First, speech does not deviate from the proper measure;
second, speech is always beneficial;
third, speech necessarily accords with principle.
Fourth, his speech is exquisite;
fifth, his speech is readily accepted;
sixth, his speech is trustworthy.
Seventh, their speech is beyond reproach;
eighth, their speech is entirely delightful.

These are the eight. If one can dedicate these toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, then upon attaining Buddhahood in the future, they will be fully endowed with the Tathāgata’s mark of the Brahma-voice.
"Furthermore, Dragon King!
If one abstains from frivolous speech, one will achieve three kinds of certainty.
What are these three?
First, he will certainly be beloved by the wise;
second, he will certainly be able to answer questions according to reality through his wisdom;
third, he will certainly possess the most supreme majesty and virtue among humans and devas, being free from all falsehood.

These are the three; if one can dedicate them toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, then when one later attains Buddhahood, all the various prophecies (*vyākaraṇa*) bestowed by the Tathāgatas shall never be in vain.
"Furthermore, Dragon King!
If one is free from lustful desire, one will achieve five kinds of mastery. What are these five?
First, mastery over the three karmas, because all sense faculties are fully complete;
second, mastery over material wealth, because no enemies or thieves can seize it;
third, mastery over merit and virtue, because all things are provided according to one's heart's desire.
Fourth, one attains sovereignty over the royal throne because all rare and wondrous objects were offered as tribute;
fifth, the goods obtained exceed one's original expectations by a hundredfold or more because of freedom from stinginess and envy in the past.

These are the five; if one can dedicate them toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, then when they later attain Buddhahood, they will be uniquely honored within the three realms, and all shall together revere and support them.
"Furthermore, Dragon King!
If one is free from ill will, one immediately attains eight kinds of mental states of joy.
What are these eight?
First, a mind free from harm and affliction;
second, a mind free from anger and resentment;
third, a mind free from contention and dispute.
4. A mind that is gentle, pliant, and straightforward;
5. Attaining the compassionate mind of a noble one;
6. Constantly cultivating a mind that benefits and brings peace to sentient beings.
Seventh, their physical appearance will be upright and majestic, and they will be respected by all;
eighth, because of their harmony and patience, they will quickly be reborn in the Brahma world.

These are the eight. If one can dedicate these merits toward Anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, then upon attaining Buddhahood in the future, they will possess an unimpeded mind that those who behold them will never tire of seeing.
"Furthermore, Dragon King!
If one is free from wrong views, one will achieve ten meritorious qualities. What are these ten?
First, attaining a truly wholesome intention and true, virtuous companions;
second, having deep faith in cause and effect, never committing evil even at the cost of one's life;
third, taking refuge in the Buddha alone, and not in other deities.
Fourth, with a straightforward mind and right view, they are forever free from the web of doubts regarding all matters of fortune and misfortune;
fifth, they are constantly reborn among humans and devas, never again falling into the evil realms;
sixth, their immeasurable merit and wisdom increase ever more excellently.
7. To be forever free from wrong paths and to practice the noble path;
8. Not to give rise to the view of a self-existent body and to abandon all evil karma;
9. To abide in unimpeded vision; 10. Not to fall into the various states of misfortune.

These are the ten; if one can dedicate them toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, then upon attaining Buddhahood in the future, one will swiftly realize all Buddha-dharmas and achieve mastery over supernatural powers (*abhijñā*).
At that time, the World-Honored One again addressed the Dragon King, saying:

"If there is a bodhisattva who, relying on these wholesome karmas, is able to practice giving while remaining free from killing during the cultivation of the Path, they will always be rich in wealth and treasures, such that none can plunder them;
they will enjoy long life without premature death, and shall not be harmed by any enemies or thieves."
Because they practice giving while abstaining from taking what is not given, they are always wealthy with treasures that cannot be plundered;
being most excellent and peerless, they are able to fully assemble the treasury of all Buddha-dharmas.
Because he practices giving while abstaining from unchaste conduct, he is always wealthy with treasures that no one can plunder;
his household is upright and harmonious, and neither his mother nor his wife and children ever look upon him with lustful intent.
Because they practice giving while abstaining from false speech, they are always rich in wealth and treasures, which no one can plunder;
being free from all slander and upholding the True Dharma, whatever they undertake will surely bear fruit according to their vows.
Because one practices giving while abstaining from divisive speech, one will always be wealthy with treasures that cannot be plundered;
one's kin and retinue will be harmonious, sharing the same aspirations and joys, and will never experience discord or strife.
Because he practices giving while abstaining from harsh speech, he is always wealthy with treasures that cannot be plundered;
all assemblies joyfully take refuge in him, and his words are received with faith by all, with none who oppose or reject them.
Because he practices giving while abstaining from meaningless speech, he is always wealthy with treasures that no one can plunder;
his words are never uttered in vain, so all people respectfully accept them; and being skilled in expedient means, he is able to sever all doubts.
Because they practice giving with a mind free from craving and seeking, they are always wealthy in treasures and riches that no one can plunder;
they relinquish all possessions through wisdom, possess firm faith and understanding, and are endowed with great majestic power.
Because one practices giving while free from a mind of anger, one will always be wealthy with treasures that cannot be plundered;
one will swiftly achieve for oneself the unimpeded wisdom-mind, with all faculties well-adorned and beautiful, such that all who see one feel respect and affection.
Because they practice giving while free from perverted views, they are always wealthy with treasures that no one can plunder;
they are constantly born into families of right view and reverent faith, where they see the Buddha, hear the Dharma, and make offerings to the Sangha, never forgetting the mind of great bodhicitta.
This is the great benefit obtained when a Mahāsattva, while practicing the bodhisattva path, cultivates the ten wholesome karmas and adorns them with generosity.
"O Dragon King!

To state the essentials: by practicing the ten paths of wholesome action and being adorned with precepts, one can give rise to all the meanings and benefits of the Buddha-dharma and fulfill great vows;
by being adorned with patience, one attains the Buddha’s perfect voice and is endowed with the various marks and signs of excellence;
by being adorned with diligence, one is able to destroy the enmity of Māra and enter the treasury of the Buddha-dharma.
Because of the adornment of meditative concentration (*samādhi*), one is able to give rise to mindfulness, wisdom, shame, remorse, and pliancy (*praśrabdhi*);
because of the adornment of wisdom (*prajñā*), one is able to sever all conceptual constructions and false views;
because of the adornment of loving-kindness (*maitrī*), one does not give rise to affliction or harm toward sentient beings.
Because of the adornment of compassion, he takes pity on all sentient beings and never tires of or abandons them;
because of the adornment of joy, when seeing those who cultivate goodness, his mind is free from resentment or envy;
because of the adornment of equanimity, toward favorable or adverse circumstances, he has no heart of attachment or aversion.
Because they are adorned with the four means of integration (*saṃgrahavastu*), they constantly and diligently gather and transform all sentient beings;
because they are adorned with the foundations of mindfulness (*smṛtyupasthāna*), they are skillfully able to practice the contemplation of the four foundations of mindfulness;
because they are adorned with the right efforts (*samyakpradhāna*), they are fully able to sever all unwholesome dharmas and accomplish all wholesome dharmas.
Because of the adornment of the bases of supernormal power (*ṛddhipāda*), they constantly bring about physical and mental pliancy and bliss;

because of the adornment of the five faculties (*indriya*), their deep faith is firm, they are diligent and untiring, they are never deluded or forgetful, they are tranquil and well-disciplined, and they sever all afflictions (*kleśa*);
because of the adornment of the powers (*bala*), all enmities are utterly extinguished, and none can cause them harm.
Because they are adorned with the factors of enlightenment (*bodhyaṅga*), they always skillfully awaken to all phenomena;
because they are adorned with the right path, correct wisdom is constantly present before them;
and because they are adorned with tranquility (*śamatha*), they are able to completely wash away all fetters and afflictions (*saṃyojana*).
Because of the adornment of contemplation, one is able to know the intrinsic nature of all phenomena as they truly are;
because of the adornment of skillful means, one swiftly attains the fulfillment of conditioned and unconditioned bliss.
“Dragon King!
You should know that these ten wholesome karmas can even cause the ten powers, the fearlessnesses, and all eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha to be fully perfected.”
Therefore, you all should practice and study with diligence!
O Dragon King!
It is just as all cities and villages depend upon the great earth to remain securely established.
All medicinal herbs, flowers, trees, and forests likewise grow by depending upon the earth.

This path of the ten wholesome actions is also like this: all humans and devas are established upon it; and all the enlightenment of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, all the practices of bodhisattvas, and all the Buddha-dharmas, are collectively accomplished by depending upon this great earth of the ten wholesome actions.

When the Buddha had finished preaching this sutra, the Dragon King Sāgara and the great assembly—including all the devas, humans, asuras, and others in the world—were filled with great joy; they believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
The Scripture on the Ten Paths of Wholesome Action (Daśakuśalakarmapatha-sūtra)
